source_text: I have a better idea than summarising.  Let's use the Evidence Landscape.  HEADs are supposed to be in my words.  So, what we'd be able to do for those missions that were created since we started recording in the Evidence Landscape is go find when they were recorded and see what words of mine were associated with that.  Two limitations are worth considering: #1 Evidence only started getting recorded after a while, so older missions wouldn't have the operator turns available; #2 Some missions are created by agents and would be less likely to have operator turns directly associated with them.  Both of these limitations are not blockers at all, I'm just saying we wouldn't expect to get complete coverage using this technique.  But if we got, say, 70 missions with real HEADs this way, then we could run the system without it being a facade, and we could figure out how to get the other missions ready.  NB similar concepts apply to Excursions and Tickets.

reply_text:
I have started a pilot of your idea on ten missions, with zai-1. My first rough measurement suggests coverage from this route will be well under 70, unless the evidence store reaches further back than the turn files on disk.

**What I measured first,** by joining each mission file's creation date in git against the stored operator turns on disk:

- The stored turn files hold 4,654 dated operator turns, from 22 August to today.
- Of the 184 missions without a HEAD, 173 were created before 22 August. Most are from May to July.
- 11 were created since then. 5 of those are named in one of your turns, and the other 6 have turns of yours in the six hours before creation.
- 13 of the older missions are named in a later turn of yours.

So from the turn files alone, roughly 11 missions could have your words from the time of creation, and about 13 more have something you said later.

**What I have not established.** Those files are one source. The evidence store itself is much larger: its text index has about 374,000 documents, and mission names occur hundreds of times (104 for M-distributed-proofreaders, 267 for M-formal-patterns). I do not know how far back your turns go in the store. If they go back to May, coverage could be far better. Finding that out is part of the pilot.

**The pilot, dispatched to zai-1.** Ten missions, five created since 22 August and five earlier. For each:

- when it was created and who committed it;
- your words associated with it, from the evidence store first, then the turn files, then turns in the same session just before creation even if they do not name it;
- the passages quoted verbatim, each with its evidence id and timestamp; no paraphrase, no tidying;
- a class: your words clearly commission it; your words exist but later or partial; turns nearby but not about it; nothing recorded.

No mission file is edited, and no HEAD is invented where there is nothing. Store queries are sequential, capped at four per mission and 50 results each.

- Job: `invoke-1790782969778-29195-fa6c203a`
- Park: `park-eb4e69df-1978-4ea6-a583-c3b8904cafa5`, 90-minute deadline

I will show you the ten before anything is written into a mission file. If it works, it scales in batches of about ten with a check between, and the same method applies to excursions and tickets.

This replaces the agent-summary proposal from my earlier message; I have dropped that.

**Still running:** Codex-4's queue (ticket and proposal sources, template-only HEAD, the wide-cascade guard) and Codex-6's Lean corrections.

**Still with you:** whether a cascade may be an unordered bag attempted all at once, which C scores the cascades, and the restart.
